column1: # docs/tasks/artifacts/canvas_spike/results.tsv — the measurements G1-SLICE.13 records. A verdict is scoped to what is below.
# Measured by bash docs/tasks/artifacts/canvas_spike/run_canvas_spike.sh browser, and the same with native.
# Hardware: Mac mini, Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB. OS: macOS 27.0.1. Browser: Google Chrome 156.0.8078.80, headless, adapter apple metal-3.
# Native webview: the system WKWebView through wry 0.53.5 and tao 0.34.8. Native GPU: wgpu 27.0.1 on Metal.
# Corpus: crates/sc-viewport corpus(7), the declared 16 pieces of 400 vertices, 14 annotations each, 200 pick and 200 snap probes. No deviation.
# Canvas: 1600 by 1000 pixels, 4x multisampled for the GPU renderers. 600 frames of scripted zoom and pan through the ladder.
# capable means it ran here. WINDOWS AND LINUX WERE NOT RUN: no machine for either exists in this setup, so the decision record's
# three-OS capability gate is unproven for all five rows. Hosted Linux has no display or GPU. R1 reopens if either OS refuses a topology.
# frame_p95_ms: time until one frame's whole picture can be read back, which no real frame needs, so it overestimates all of them.
# Waiting for the display is excluded. WKWebView's timer has 1 ms steps, so its two rows move between 3 and 6 ms across runs; Chrome's has 0.1 ms.
# peak_mb: physical footprint from top in a visit with no read-backs, which adds up the browser's processes. Webview rows add WebKit's helpers.
# unproven_deps: a judgment. 0 the platform canvas; 1 WebGPU in a browser, wry for a webview; 2 both; 3 wgpu, tao and wry composing a surface with a webview.
# fidelity_max_px: where a marker's pixels actually landed, by centroid, against the exact position, over 9 zooms and 5 points.
# Two runs agreed within those steps. These rows are the second run. One machine and one sample each: not a performance claim about any other machine.
